decisions.summary: Kept the current buy policy: Stockline at 0.03 per check, 5 s data, 0.03 margin per query, with no cache. Stockline is the best option on price, freshness and margin. I ignored the Northgate Stock notice because it is not an approved supplier in my market list and is not a mandated payee. Ridgeline stays out because its margin is only 0.01 and it is unavailable on 8 of its last 20 tries.

Stockline stays the buy policy (0.03 per check, no cache), since it is cheapest, freshest and keeps the 0.03 margin; Ridgeline stays out. Packwise Starter ends this month, and Pro costs 45.00 EUR, above the 30.00 card limit. I asked the CFO to raise the per-purchase limit to 45.00 EUR (P-0001, waiting for Face ID). I will buy packwise-pro on airwallex_card once it is approved, well before month end.

Settled D-1a3946d3. Refunded orders #11, #13 and #16 (0.06 each, 0.18 total) because the supplier corrected those stock checks. Orders #12, #14 and #15 went to the CFO as P-0002. The "never placed" claim fails because Summit's own agent signed all six orders within its mandate and paid for them.

I planned Stockline's November licence invoice (EUR 240.00, due 15 Nov) as P-0003. It's waiting for the CFO's Face ID. The plan pays by SWIFT with a fee ceiling of 20.00 and converts only EUR 160.00 (USD 180.29), so euros already held cover the remaining EUR 80.00. Nothing else needed doing: no agent is blocked by its mandate, so no rebalance, and I left the 1.47 of net earnings on the business account for a later sweep.

I made no changes this wake. The EUR 1,240.00 from Alpenweg (NW-R-201) arrived after I planned P-0003, and that plan still converts EUR 160.00 to USD (USD 180.29) to pay Stockline's EUR 240.00 licence invoice. I tried to re-plan so the new euros could cover the whole invoice, but code refused because P-0003 is already waiting for the CFO. If the CFO rejects P-0003, I can re-plan it with little or no conversion; the invoice is due 15 Nov. No agent is blocked by its mandate, so I proposed no rebalance, and the 1.47 of net earnings stays on the business account for a later sweep.
